newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania seeks new S&P rating ahead of bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania seeks new S&P rating ahead of bond issue.

text.p: Lithuania is seeking a new credit rating, this time from Standard & Poor's, and S&P officials have already met Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius and other officials, the finance ministry said on Friday.
Lithuania wants the rating ahead of a planned $200 million eurobond issue and hopes it will be higher than ratings given by IBCA and Moodys.
"Standard & Poor's are working in the country now," Ruta Skyriene, deputy head of the finance ministry international department, told Reuters.
S&P experts had meetings with Vagnorius, central bank and finance ministry officials on Thursday.
"Considering that the government of Lithuania is accelerating reforms, Lithuania may be given an investment grade in line with Latvia," one financial analysis said.

Latvia was assigned an S&P BBB rating in January. European credit rating agency IBCA assigned a BB+ long-term foreign currency rating to Lithuania in January, one notch higher than U.S Moody's rating of Ba2 in September last year.
